item.title: Mount Tsukuba: Twin Peaks & Cable Car Views Over the Kanto Plain — Guide
item.description: Mount Tsukuba, despite standing just 877 m tall, is ranked among Japan’s 100 famous mountains, its distinctive twin peaks (male and female summits) rising dramatically from the flat Kanto plain, visible from a striking distance. A cable car and separate ropeway make the summit accessible without a demanding hike, leading to observation points with panoramic views that, on exceptionally clear days, stretch as far as Tokyo Skytree and Mount Fuji. Hiking trails also wind up the mountain for those preferring to climb on foot.

item.title: Tsukuba Mineral Spa Resort: Hot Springs at the Foot of the Mountain — Guide
item.description: The mineral spa resorts clustered at the foot of Mount Tsukuba draw on naturally mineral-rich waters to offer a relaxing wellness experience for visitors who have spent the day hiking or sightseeing on the mountain. Several facilities offer day-use bathing (higaeri onsen) with views toward Tsukuba’s distinctive peaks, along with saunas, massage services and restaurants, making the area a comfortable base for combining outdoor activity with genuine relaxation. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Tsukuba, Ibaraki Hours Day baths typically 10:00–21:00, facility-dependent Admission Day bath from ~¥800–1,500 Time needed 1.
